title: Handle a press crisis
summary: Verify before you respond. Collect what is actually said, separate factual errors from unfavorable-but-true reporting, and timestamp the spread; the response to a wrong fact and the response to a true story are different moves. One spokesperson speaks; everyone else routes inquiries and posts nothing. For factual errors, request corrections through the outlet's own channel with the evidence attached; newsroom ethics codes commit journalists to prompt correction (the SPJ code is the reference). Any statement touching a dispute, a regulator, or a named individual goes through legal review first; the statement outlives the news cycle. Respond once, factually, in one place, and link to it everywhere else; arguing in every thread refreshes the story. Tell customers and the team the same thing you told the public. Monitoring is agent work; the judgment calls are not. Nothing here is legal advice.

parts.title: Verify before responding: collect the claims, separate factual errors from unfavorable-but-true reporting, and timestamp the spread

execution.rationale: Compile the coverage and threads from supplied links into a dated claims table, marking which statements are factually wrong, which are contested, and which are true.

parts.title: Name one spokesperson; everyone else routes inquiries there and posts nothing

execution.rationale: The founder names the single spokesperson and tells the team where inquiries route and that nobody else engages publicly.

parts.title: Stand up monitoring: alerts and feeds for the story's spread, so responses track reality rather than anxiety

execution.rationale: Google Alerts and the Google News RSS feeds provide documented monitoring for the company's name and the story's keywords; results compile into the claims table.

parts.title: For factual errors, request corrections through the outlet's own channel, with the evidence attached

references.title: SPJ Code of Ethics (accuracy and corrections)

execution.rationale: The spokesperson contacts the outlet's corrections channel with the documents that establish the error; newsroom ethics codes commit members to prompt correction.

parts.title: Legal review before any public statement that touches a dispute, a regulator, or a named individual

execution.rationale: Counsel reviews the draft statement for admissions, defamation exposure, and conflicts with any live dispute before it is published.

parts.title: Respond once, factually, in one place; link to it everywhere else rather than arguing in every thread

execution.rationale: The spokesperson publishes the single reviewed response and points every other channel at it; replying thread-by-thread refreshes the story.

parts.title: Tell customers and the team the same thing you told the public

execution.rationale: The founder briefs the team and affected customers with the published statement so the inside version cannot leak differently.

parts.title: Let the cycle pass: keep monitoring, correct new factual errors, and write the postmortem

execution.rationale: The spokesperson watches the monitoring feeds through the cycle, handles follow-ups, and records what the company will do differently.

metadata.trigger: A negative story is live and spreading: press coverage, a viral thread, or a review pile-on names your company.
metadata.supportReason: Claim verification and monitoring run as agent work from supplied links and alert feeds; the spokesperson role, the correction requests, legal review, and the single public response are human calls.

contextNeeded.query: links to the coverage and threads, with timestamps
the facts in dispute, with the documents that prove or correct them
